scope: Independent content, notation, source-claim, caption-alignment and educational-mathematics review of the final manuscript. Image production, source-rights clearance, browser QA, CI and publication status are outside this review.

checks.evidence: Reused actual provider-returned 2,115-segment manual-labelled zh-TW track; 183 context segments selected and reviewed. The article identifies page 6 as the same recap context used for chapter 14, not a distinct verified page-change frame or spoken reading of its prompt screenshots.

Source PDF pages 7–10 visually distinguish lowercase harness h from uppercase human-information H in L(A_{theta,h}, H). Article uses h and H_info and keeps theta fixed only in the specified harness examples.
Displayed R-Zero/AZR prompt goals and output constraints are described as design instructions, not measured human accuracy, guaranteed difficulty or guaranteed valid output.

The source slide red question marks and captions at 399.432–427.760 s frame differentiability as a difficulty. Article does not present that expression as a ready-to-run optimizer for arbitrary prompts, code and branches.

Article says the proposing model may be the target itself or a separate fixed model, matching captions 427.760–446.679 s. q_phi is a pedagogical generator; generating a candidate does not imply training phi or theta.

Internal L and final human target Lhat are separated, matching captions 459.192–473.272 s. Article states that observed development-score selection does not guarantee expected or held-out improvement, and reused selection tasks are not an independent final evaluation.
ACI design and fixed-model comparisons are separated from autonomous harness invention. Human analysis and configuration sweep now cite PDF page 5 section 4 separately from the ACI description.

Final ICLR 2024 paper supports optimizing program demonstrations and prompts as well as weight finetuning. Article restricts its fixed-theta example rather than claiming the whole framework never updates weights.

Paper pages 5–7 fix model, temperature and output format in its practical search, while modifying prompts and code connections. The article distinguishes MCTS nodes containing entire workflows from LLM-call nodes, and experience/score propagation from neural gradient backpropagation.

Paper pages 4–5 define all-k success versus at-least-one success for same-task i.i.d. trials and task-wise averages. Article uses the finite combination estimators, differentiates plug-in powers, and identifies Figure 4 as the historical 2024 tau-retail result.
Article retains the source warning that matching the final database and outputs can miss some policy violations such as omitted confirmation; repeated success is relative to the stated scorer.

All three example groups are labelled fictional. Paired gains, feasible token-budget choice, incremental token calculation, search-plus-execution total and reliability estimators pass the independent exact checks.

resolved_review_items.resolution: Retained the ACI citation and added a separate section 4 / PDF page 5 citation for human behavioral analysis and configuration search.
Explicitly states that the proposer may be the target model itself or a separate fixed model; no proposer-weight-training claim.

limits: Caption timings are spoken-topic anchors, not frame-verified slide transitions. Page 6 intentionally overlaps the preceding chapter recap.
The full caption response was retained, but only the selected 183 context segments were reviewed for this chapter.
The source PDF pages were visually inspected; final generated assets and browser screenshots are handled by separate reviews.
Arithmetic checks verify invented examples and specified statistical assumptions, not reported benchmark reproduction.
